content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge rules a link UNDERDETERMINED and grounds that ruling on what a single verse, Matthew 1:16, admits, which is the kind of single-verse ground the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.", "room": "Whether 'admits both readings' of Matthew 1:16 is a ground about the verse's wording or a weighing of the whole chain of rows; I read it as the former, because the judge's stated ground is the verse's grammar and the rebuttals are cited only as answers to it.", "why": "The judge makes UNDERDETERMINED turn on the single verse Matthew 1:16 admitting two readings, which is a single-verse ground the rule forbids."}
